drills.title: Defensive line · Whistle then advance together
drills.objective: Build the simplest defensive-line reaction: on a coach's whistle all six U10 defenders move two short steps forward together, preserve their spacing, then hold their shape. Use this before the carry-or-pass decision drill.
drills.safety: Non-contact reaction drill. Keep a clear run-off and stop the line well before the coach or attacker. The whistle is a coach's practice cue, not a substitute for checking current RFU U10 offside and restart requirements. Never treat this as permission to rush a free pass from an illegal starting position.

frames.name: Set up · six defenders connected
frames.notes: Six defenders form a line at even spacing. The coach stays in the same position as in the later carry-or-pass drill. Explain: react to the whistle together, then stop square and balanced. The attacker and ground ball stay still.

frames.name: Whistle · advance two short steps together
frames.notes: The coach blows the whistle. All six defenders step forward immediately and in unison, without sprinting into contact. Eyes up, spacing unchanged. They must be legally onside before moving in a real restart.

frames.name: Hold shape · look and communicate
frames.notes: Pause and check that the line is still connected, everyone is facing the play and nobody has sprinted out alone. Repeat several times before adding a ball-carrier decision.

drills.players: Six defenders (D1–D6), one support attacker (A1), one coach/ball feeder. Start with all six defenders across the same line. The coach and A1 are behind them, with A1 slightly deeper to receive.
drills.equipment: One rugby ball. The saved 10 × 20 m practice area uses boundary flags; no separate cones or contact pads are shown. For a real session, mark the area safely using the available training equipment.
drills.instructions: 1. Set out the six-defender line as shown. Coach and supporting runner remain in their starting positions. 2. Explain that this is a whistle-reaction exercise, not permission to cross an offside line. 3. Blow the whistle and ask every defender to advance two short steps together. 4. Stop, check spacing and communication, reset, then repeat. 5. Progress to Hold the line · Carry or pass? after the group can move together.
drills.coaching: Coach the timing of the FIRST step, not an all-out sprint. Keep shoulders square, communication short and the line connected. Use the pause to ask who moved early or late. Keep all actions non-contact. At a real U10 free pass, ensure the defenders have retired the required distance and only advance when lawfully permitted.
drills.regression: Start with slower calls and two small steps. Stop if any defender sprints ahead or loses spacing.
drills.progression: Next: Hold the line · Carry or pass? (seed-133). The same defensive line and coach position now develop into two decision outcomes.
drills.questions: Did all six move on the whistle together? Was there a gap after the first step? Can you say which teammate you must stay connected with?
drills.notes: This is the introductory, linear whistle-and-advance drill, not a branching decision. Play it before Hold the line · Carry or pass? to teach the same connected line and short first step. The whistle is a coaching cue; defenders must respect age-grade offside and restart rules in a real game.

drills.title: Hold the line · Carry or pass?
drills.objective: Defenders move together, scan for the ball carrier and close the right channel without losing the line. The attack has a genuine choice: the coach carries, or passes backwards to A1.
drills.safety: U10 activity: begin with touch for both outcomes. Never ask children to tackle an adult coach. The adult-carry outcome is always a two-hand touch demonstration. If practising the A1 tackle, use only age-matched participants with an appropriately qualified coach, a progressive tackle warm-up, controlled speed and the current RFU tackle-height requirement. Head to the safe side, stable feet, shoulder-and-arm connection, and a complete wrap—not a head-first or diving contact. D5 is a covering defender, not a second simultaneous tackler. Stop immediately if spacing or head position becomes unsafe; the player who goes to ground must release and present safely. Confirm current RFU Regulation 15 Appendix 4 before the session.

frames.name: Set up · six defenders and two attackers
frames.notes: Six defenders start connected across the pitch. Coach and A1 stand behind the ball. The four cones mark a working area; A1 begins deeper so the eventual pass can travel backwards.

frames.name: Coach collects the ball
frames.notes: Coach picks up the grounded ball. Defenders stay ready and communicate their spacing; A1 waits deeper for a possible pass.

frames.name: WHISTLE · GO — read the carrier
frames.notes: The whistle starts the movement. Coach runs towards the defensive line, while all six defenders take small steps up together. At the yellow diamond, STOP and choose A or B.

decision.question: Open gap?
decision.cue: Look on defense movement to spot possible gaps.

options.label: Coach carries · D1 and D2 close for touch
Coach passes · A1 attacks D4's channel

frames.name: B1 · Backwards pass to A1
frames.notes: Coach passes backwards across to A1, who stays deeper until the ball arrives. D4 calls the receiver; D5 covers the neighbouring channel while the remaining defenders stay connected.

frames.name: B2 · A1 attacks; D4 tackles
frames.notes: A1 receives, looks up and carries into the outside channel. D4 tracks A1, shortens steps and makes the controlled tackle using safe head placement and a wrap. D5 closes the adjacent gap as cover; D5 does not join the tackle.

frames.name: B3 · Release and present
frames.notes: D4 releases and gets back to feet. A1 goes to ground safely, releases and presents the ball away from pressure. D5 stays on feet and does not dive into the contact area. Reset the players and repeat with the other outcome.

drills.players: Six defenders (D1–D6), one support attacker (A1), one coach/ball feeder. Start with all six defenders across the same line. The coach and A1 are behind them, with A1 slightly deeper to receive.
drills.equipment: One rugby ball. The saved 10 × 20 m practice area uses boundary flags; no separate cones or contact pads are shown. For a real session, mark the area safely using the available training equipment.
drills.instructions:
Set up D1–D6 in a connected defensive line. The ball begins on the ground by the coach; A1 waits deeper and to the opposite side. On the whistle, defenders take a few controlled steps forward together. The coach runs towards the line and a decision is reached. PAUSE: choose A or B.
A — Carry: the coach keeps the ball and runs into the near-side channel. D1 and D2 close the space and make a two-hand TOUCH on the adult coach. Stop and reset.
B — Pass: the coach passes backwards to A1. D4 tracks A1 into the outside channel and completes a controlled tackle; D5 closes the space as cover, not as a simultaneous second tackler. A1 releases and presents the ball. Reset to the same start after either option.
Try both outcomes. For the players, avoid announcing which option the coach will choose until the defenders have started moving.
drills.coaching:
DEFENCE — Go together on GO, not six separate sprints. Look across the line and talk: 'UP', 'BALL', 'MY SIDE'. Shorten steps as the carrier approaches. The closest player tracks the hips; the next defender covers the space beside them. Everyone else stays connected and watches for the pass.
ATTACK — Pick up securely, eyes up and choose space. When passing, keep A1 behind the carrier and send the ball backwards. A1 catches before accelerating; keep the ball available after a legal tackle.
Keep the tempo modest. One good read and one good call are more valuable than a big collision.
drills.regression: First walk it through with defenders knowing the option. Use two-hand touch on every carrier, keep the pass simple and allow a verbal pause so the defenders can identify their responsibilities.
drills.progression: Do not reveal A or B until the coach reaches the decision. Vary the channel, move the receiving attacker to a new starting position (still behind for the pass), or shorten the time defenders have to communicate. Increase pace only after the defensive line stays organised; contact is a separate technical progression.
drills.questions: Who noticed the ball changing hands first? Did all six defenders move up together? Which two players were responsible for the channel, and who kept the line connected? Was the pass backwards? Could you stop the run with safe positioning rather than a rushed hit?
drills.notes: This drill contains two real playable outcomes after a shared whistle and defensive advance. Playback stops at the diamond. Choose A or B and the animation continues with different ball possession and defender reactions. The standard video export plays A and B in labelled chapters; the coaching sheet shows both. The illustrations are coach-authored examples, not automatic tactical predictions or official RFU material.

branching.question: Ball carrier's choice: carry into the gap or pass to A1?

choices.label: Coach carries · D1 and D2 close for touch

frames.name: A1 · Carry into the near-side channel
frames.notes: Coach keeps the ball and accelerates through the near-side gap. D1 calls the carrier, D2 covers the inside, and the other defenders remain connected. D1 and D2 stop the adult coach with two-hand touch only.

frames.name: A2 · Two-hand touch · stop and reset
frames.notes: Freeze when D1 and D2 have closed the channel. Count the touch; do not make a live tackle on the adult. Ask who called the ball and whether the rest of the line stayed connected.

choices.explanation: The coach keeps the ball and carries into the inside channel. The nearest two defenders close the gap and finish with two-hand touch. Children must not tackle an adult coach.
choices.watchFor: D1 and D2 communicate, close space without diving in and hold the inside. The other defenders keep their channels rather than chasing the coach.

choices.label: Coach passes · A1 attacks D4's channel

frames.name: B1 · Backwards pass to A1
frames.notes: Coach passes backwards across to A1, who stays deeper until the ball arrives. D4 calls the receiver; D5 covers the neighbouring channel while the remaining defenders stay connected.

frames.name: B2 · A1 attacks; D4 tackles
frames.notes: A1 receives, looks up and carries into the outside channel. D4 tracks A1, shortens steps and makes the controlled tackle using safe head placement and a wrap. D5 closes the adjacent gap as cover; D5 does not join the tackle.

frames.name: B3 · Release and present
frames.notes: D4 releases and gets back to feet. A1 goes to ground safely, releases and presents the ball away from pressure. D5 stays on feet and does not dive into the contact area. Reset the players and repeat with the other outcome.

choices.explanation: The coach passes backwards to A1. The outside defenders track the new ball carrier, with one controlled age-matched tackler and a covering defender in the demonstration.
choices.watchFor: Watch the backward pass, D4's approach to the ball carrier and D5's covering position. The tackle must be controlled and supervised by a qualified coach.

branching.context: The first movement is the same in both cases: the defensive line advances together on the whistle. The choice comes when the ball is played. Defenders must identify the actual carrier before changing their shape.
branching.watchFor: Look at the first two steps: are all six defenders moving on the same cue, with their spacing intact? Then watch which defenders communicate and adjust to the carrier.

drills.title: U10 · Tackle, release and present to support
drills.players: 3 players per repetition: A1 carrier, D1 defender, A2 support; one qualified supervising coach.
drills.equipment: 1 rugby ball, 4 cones; a clear 10 × 8 m working area.
drills.objective: Show an ordinary U10 tackle sequence: track under control, bring the carrier to ground, release promptly, present the ball backwards and collect it from the support side.
drills.safety: Coach-led demonstration only. Begin at walking speed with no contact, then add controlled tackle contact only under a suitably qualified club coach and the current RFU U10 Rules of Play. Keep the area clear; no diving, high contact or head-first entry. Stop if players lose control. The animation explains sequence and ball location, not physical tackle technique.
drills.instructions: Use four cones to mark a small 10 × 8 m working area. Place A1 and D1 facing each other, with A2 several steps behind A1. Run the sequence in the displayed order: (1) track and close; (2) controlled tackle; (3) D1 releases promptly and moves clear while A1 presents the ball towards A2; (4) A2 arrives on feet and collects the ball from the support side; (5) carry away and reset. Swap player roles between repetitions. Start without actual contact until the coach is satisfied with the positioning.
drills.coaching:
Track: watch the carrier, shorten steps and keep the approach controlled.
Tackle: coach contact position and safe technique off-animation; no diving or high contact.
Release: the tackler must let go and get clear promptly.
Present: the grounded ball carrier makes the ball available back towards supporting teammates, not towards the defender.
Support: arrive from your own side, on your feet; pick up only while the ball is available and no ruck has formed.
Play: move the ball away and reset. Pause the presentation step to ask children which side the ball belongs on.
drills.regression: Use a no-contact walk-through: D1 tags/indicates the tackle, A1 kneels/lowers to a controlled grounded pose and presents the ball; A2 collects without an opposing contest. Repeat the sequence before any live tackling.
drills.progression: Once your qualified coach approves, increase the approach speed slightly, vary the defender's starting angle or have A2 choose an appropriate supporting line. Keep one tackle pair and one support runner in the confined area.
drills.questions: Who must release after the tackle? Why does A1 place the ball towards A2? Which direction is the support side? When can A2 pick up the ball? What changes if a ruck has already formed?
drills.notes: Standard Classic-editor drill data (players, one rugby ball, tackle marker, ordinary pose changes and ball transfer). No special test-only rendering or scripted sprites. Read the coaching notes before attempting contact; the animation is a visual sequence, not technical instruction.

frames.name: Set up · one carrier, one defender, one support
frames.notes: A1 has the ball. D1 faces the runner from a controlled distance. A2 waits behind A1 as support. Coach positions the pair before the demonstration.

frames.name: Track and close the distance
frames.notes: A1 carries forwards. D1 tracks from in front, shortens the steps and stays balanced. A2 advances behind the ball carrier. Start with a controlled, low-speed rehearsal.

frames.name: Tackle · controlled contact and ground
frames.notes: Pause at contact: show only the player-on-player positioning and the ball carrier going to ground. Teach actual tackle mechanics separately under qualified supervision.

frames.name: Release immediately · present towards A2
frames.notes: D1 releases and moves away. A1 stays fully grounded and places the ball back towards A2, NOT forward towards the defender. Watch the ball travel just beyond the grounded player's hands.

frames.name: Support arrives on feet from the correct side
frames.notes: A2 approaches the presented ball from behind while remaining on their feet. D1 stays clear. The ball remains stationary on the ground until the support player takes it.

frames.name: A2 collects the available ball
frames.notes: With no ruck formed and the defender released, A2 picks up from their own side. A1 begins to recover. Show the separate ball attaching only when it is actually collected.

frames.name: Play away and reset
frames.notes: A2 carries away into space. A1 regains their feet and clears the area; D1 resets. Rotate the carrier and defender roles for the next supervised repetition.

drills.title: U10 | Tackle, secure and go again
drills.objective: Retain possession after a tackle: present the ball, recognise the first defender at the breakdown, support from the correct side and move the ball into space for a second phase.
drills.safety: Coach-led, age-appropriate progression only. First rehearse at walking pace with touch or no-contact representation; progress to controlled contact only when qualified coaching and player readiness allow. Check surface, space, equipment, club guidance and consent/readiness. Use the shield as a passive visual or controlled-contact aid only if permitted by the club’s age-grade and safeguarding guidance; never charge into it or through a grounded player. Stop immediately for unsafe head/neck position, loss of balance or pain. No diving, squeeze ball, neck rolls, lifting or hand-offs. U10: original carrier/tackler plus one arriving player per side at the breakdown; when the ball is secured, use it within five seconds of the referee’s call. No hands in a formed ruck for the arriving player in this scenario. After the second tackle, release and present before reset.

frames.name: Set up · two queues
frames.notes: A1 carries the ball at the head of the blue queue. D1 faces A1; D2 holds the passive shield behind D1, with D3 waiting. Show the seven cones and the route around the central line. Check spacing, roles and readiness. Allow clear space between the queues, wider start/contact gates and the central cone line. The blue group initially moves down the page.

frames.name: Approach · choose left or right
frames.notes: A1 scans the central cone line, chooses left or right and runs around it. The blue route shows the example; the thin gold route shows the other choice. A2 and A3 advance in support; D1 tracks the carrier. Pause before contact to check head up, balance and two hands on the ball.

decision.question: Which side of the cones offers space?
decision.cue: Look up, vary the angle and accelerate into space. Either side can be valid.

frames.name: First tackle · A1 and D1
frames.notes: D1 closes the remaining space and makes a controlled tackle on A1. Show the ball carrier grounded and the tackler completing the wrap. Coach checks safe tracking, head position and tackle height; stop for unsafe technique. Rehearse at walking pace before any controlled contact. The next step is immediate release and ball presentation.

frames.name: Release and present
frames.notes: D1 releases immediately and moves clear to the side. A1 makes the ball available towards the blue queue. Cue: release, present and move clear when safe; never trap the ball under the body.

frames.name: Defending support arrives
frames.notes: D2 approaches first with the shield from the defending side. A2 curves in from the blue queue; A3 stays behind. Shield is passive; coach checks a controlled approach, own-side entry and safe posture.

frames.name: Clearout · ruck formed
frames.notes: A2 meets the shield position from the attacking side. Rehearse stable feet, head and shoulders above hips and a controlled bind in live play. One arriving player per side; no charging, diving or contact through A1.

frames.name: Contest for possession
frames.notes: Pause to recognise the ruck: A2 and D2 represent opposing players on feet over the ball. No extra arrivals or hands in this formed ruck. Shield stage is a controlled representation, not a collision contest.

frames.name: Ball secured · A3 collects
frames.notes: A2 clears the ball’s access; A3 approaches from the blue side and collects only when the ball is available. D2 retreats. Cue: use it promptly; A3 stays balanced and on feet, A1 recovers when safe.

frames.name: Play away · second tackle
frames.notes: A3 carries left into the next channel and meets D3. D3 tracks and wraps at the correct height. Stop after this second tackle; release and present before reset. Original ruck is over once the ball leaves; A1/A2/D2 recover safely.

drills.players: 6 players: A1 (first carrier), A2 (first attacking support), A3 (next carrier); D1 (first tackler), D2 (passive shield holder), D3 (second defender). One supervising coach; rotate all six roles after each repetition.
drills.equipment: 1 size 4 rugby ball, 1 suitable contact shield, 7 marker cones as shown. Optional spare ball and extra boundary cones. Use a clear 20 m × 15 m practice area with runoff.
drills.instructions: Set two queues facing each other as shown, with blue attacking towards the bottom of the original diagram. Keep the seven cones in their shown arrangement. A1 reads the space and chooses a route around the central cone line. Pause to show both possibilities; the example then demonstrates a separate controlled tackle by D1. D1 releases and clears the area; A1 presents the ball towards blue support. D2 approaches first with the passive shield; A2 arrives from the attacking side and rehearses a controlled clearout. A3 stays available, collects the exposed ball when it is playable, moves left and meets D3. Stop after the second tackle and practise release/presentation before resetting. Suggested 8 min: 2 min walkthrough, 4 min coached repetitions, 2 min review/rotation. Animation seconds are illustrative, not contact targets.
drills.coaching: A1: carry securely in two hands, scan the defender, remain balanced, keep head out of the opponent’s headspace and present promptly towards support. D1/D3: track, lower under control, wrap arms and release immediately; use a tackle height below the base of the sternum. A2: arrive from own side, eyes up, stable feet, head and shoulders above hips; in live play bind before or as contact occurs. D2: hold the shield passively and follow the coach’s instructions; no collision contest. A3: stay onside, communicate, wait for a playable ball, collect with two hands and accelerate into space only when clear. Reward ball availability, safe posture, timing and decision-making rather than force.
drills.regression: Walk through with D1/D3 giving a two-hand touch; A1 lowers to the ground independently under coach instruction. D2 marks the defender position without contact; A2 demonstrates approach and stance, then A3 collects an exposed stationary ball. Increase space or pause each phase.
drills.progression: Once safe technique is established, vary the side of the first tackle and the timing of the passive defender. Ask A2 to decide whether support is needed and A3 to choose an available channel. Use controlled age-appropriate opposition only with qualified supervision; keep the same U10 participation limits. Rotate attacker/defender roles between repetitions.
drills.questions: Where should A1 put the ball? What must D1 do immediately after the tackle? Which side must A2 and D2 approach from? When is A3 allowed to pick up the ball? Where is the space for the next carry?
drills.notes: This is a six-player practice, not a match formation. D2 arrives first by design, not because defenders are required to arrive first. The shield models opposition; shield contact is not a literal live ruck bind. The first ruck marker is removed in the final diagram because the ruck ends when the ball leaves; A1, A2 and D2 recover safely. The studio’s default ATTACK arrow points up; your blue line actually attacks down initially, then A3 moves left. The setup has been re-centred, gates widened and queue spacing opened. The approach and first tackle now have separate steps. One visual decision shows the two routes around the central cones; it does not branch the animation. Confirm current RFU Appendix 4 and club policy before delivery; the 2026–27 referee summary was accessible but the direct official appendix returned 403.
